notes: SGLang structural-tag export uses ReasoningBoundary::External because SGLang owns the reasoning gate.
Aborted double-reasoning setup runs are excluded from scored configurations.
Each result retains the actual request, response and SSE timing.
The v1 batch adapter cannot express some guided/request modes; unavailable modes count separately from mismatches in supported modes.
M3 parallel invocations share one native tool_call wrapper; production grammar accepts the complete parallel sequence.
M3 XML separator whitespace is bounded to2; string-value whitespace is preserved (compiler checks).
The ai-dynamo-runtime1.5.1 distribution supplies Python package metadata only; the deployed frontend/runtime core is built from Dynamo1.6.0 commit178cc2f3f7.
provenance.deployment_adapter: Dynamo registration omits unsupported tokenizer= when constructing the pinned native ReasoningParser; parser source unchanged.

structural_tag_support.v1: M3 structural_tag_builder is None in published10.0.6; requested enable flag falls back to existing JSON/native modes.
structural_tag_support.v2: Native minimax_m3_xml where lossless; incompatible schema constraints use existing JSON guidance.
structural_tag_support.sglang: Pinned MinimaxM3Detector.supports_structural_tag() returns False. Tagged runs explicitly supply the production v2 XML constraint through response_format; the native parser remains unchanged.

findings: Approved schema replay in progress. Original 362/368 v2 score and raw model failures remain in ../2026-10-16/.
All 23 scenarios will be rerun, including both changed cases, against each backend/configuration. No previous rows will be reused.

changes: json_escaping: const equals existing expected decoded string

kernel_cache_adapter.behavior: fcntl process lock only on MSA cache misses; cache-hit fast paths and native parser source unchanged

provenance.timing_scope: Functional replay over Teleport port-forward. Concurrency4 per implementation; paired Dynamo v1/v2 runs overlap. SSE timings are observations, not isolated throughput/latency benchmark comparisons.
